title: White Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs baked in a creamy spinach and feta sauce
excerpt: White shakshuka skips the tomatoes and instead bakes eggs in a rich sauce of wilted spinach, double cream, and crumbled feta. The result is a deeply satisfying pan of food that takes 20 minutes from start to finish. Serve straight from the pan with plenty of bread for mopping.
sourceNotes: A modern variation on the Middle Eastern shakshuka tradition. The white version with cream, spinach, and feta has become popular across European and American brunch menus.

content.text: Cover the pan when cooking the eggs and keep the heat low. Uncovered or on too high a heat, the whites set before the yolks have a chance to cook through at the edges.
Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the spinach in large handfuls, stirring each batch until wilted before adding more. Once all the spinach is wilted, pour in the double cream. Stir in the nutmeg and season with salt and pepper.
Scatter two-thirds of the feta over the spinach mixture. Make 8 wells with a spoon and crack one egg into each well. Season the eggs lightly.

Cover the pan and cook over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the egg whites are set but the yolks are still runny. Scatter the remaining feta on top. Serve straight from the pan with flatbread.

items.symptom: Egg whites are set but yolks are hard.
items.fix: Check at 6 minutes and remove from heat earlier.

items.cause: Spinach was not cooked down enough.
items.fix: Cook spinach longer before adding cream.

items.cause: Feta and eggs both carry salt.
items.fix: Season very lightly at the start.
